title: Meeting Ray Charles and recording in 1953
summary: Ray visited Grunewald and requested him for the Atlantic session; Ray sent for him in 1957 as musical director.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Let me back up because I've got something here on you and Ray Charles. It seems you all did a record in 1953 together. You and his band. Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. So was that the first time you got with Ray? Yeah. Okay, because I've got this discography. It says December 4th, 1953. I've forgotten the date.
I'm busy with it during the time. And you did Don't You Know and Ray Charles Blues. Yeah.
So how did you get with Ray's band?

Well, at the school, at the Greenwald School of Music, any time some out of time musicians would come to town, the guys at the school would invite them up to be our guests, to play, either just sit down in one of the classes and make some comments. So Ray came over there and we had a jam session. So when he got ready to do the record, he requested that I play. Play trumpet. They had two trumpets, Frank Mitchell and myself. And-
Well who invited Ray over to Greenwald's? I don't know.

I don't know because- but Ray used to live here. And he was in here in and out all the time. So I don't know who asked him to come over, but he came. Sonny Stitt came in town, when he came to town, he came over there and played. All the guys when they come into town, they would come over there that Monday. Usually when they come and play, they would play on a Sunday. They'd come over to the school on Monday.
So there was like a, every Sunday there was a-

Yeah. But they didn't call it, just you called a guy to sit in. It wasn't like you're hiring somebody for a jam session. He didn't announce it was a jam session. The guy said, look we have Sonny Stitt in the house, he's going to come up and play a couple of numbers.
So Ray was invited over. What did you think about him?
Oh I thought he was great. When you heard Ray? But he didn't sing, he was just playing piano.
Yeah he was good. Well just as a player.

Well he didn't have a band, he came here with a band, Lowell Folsom. That's the band he was playing with when he came to New Orleans. Lowell Folsom played it that Sunday, and Ray came over to the school on Monday.
So like I said, what did you think of him when you heard him play? Oh I thought he was great. I thought he was great.

And then we got to know each other well and he sent for me to come to play with his band in 1957. And I played with his band and after I got there he wanted me to take over the band. Call the rehearsals, call the numbers, knock off the tunes. I played with his band about five different times. I never would stay with one band too long.
